theory: State $a\ne0$ and that the rule applies on intervals where the real-valued integrand is defined. Correct the claim that negative $a$ always makes $a(n+1)$ negative: when $n<-1$, both factors are negative and their product is positive, as practice.mastery[0] demonstrates; the sign of the primitive also depends on the bracket power and $C$. Replace the absolute prohibition on expansion with the fact that expansion is unnecessary for this rule, since expansion remains mathematically valid for nonnegative integer powers.
